title: Edge-Bridge self-serve proxy template and prioritization lanes for isolated private deploy requests
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Goal: Create a low-friction, documented self-serve pattern (Edge Bridge) and operational priority lanes so mid-market and enterprise customers requesting VPC/on-prem/air-gapped deployments can validate network readiness and receive an approved proxy template + engagement SLA. This ticket scopes the product definition, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for: 1) a downloadable/hosted Edge Bridge proxy connector template (Docker/OVF) with minimal networking prerequisites and a short preflight checklist; 2) a triage rubric that assigns priority lanes (Fastpass / Standard / Consult) based on risk signals; 3) a lightweight telemetry contract so Support/SEs see readiness signals before provisioning; and 4) integration points with intake forms and the Console onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: Edge Bridge proxy template artifact published to internal downloads (Docker image + docs) with a clear network diagram and firewall rules summary
Preflight network-check script (curl/TCP/port probes) provided with exit codes and human-readable diagnostics
Priority lane rubric documented (criteria & thresholds) and integrated into intake spreadsheet and self-serve form decisions
Console onboarding stub shows suggested lane and next steps for customers after submission
Support+SE runbook created (playbook, expected time-to-first-response per lane, escalation path)
Telemetry signals emitted (probe success/failure, proxy version, last-upgrade-patch) and visible on a lightweight dashboard link
Legal/security checklist (KMS, E2E encryption, audit log expectations) completed and signed off by Security
Security review completed and any hardening recommendations implemented in the template
Pilot with 2 customers executed (one VPC narrow-egress, one air-gapped with proxy bridge) and learnings captured
tasks: PM: draft product spec and intake form modifications (link to Confluence)
Design: create network diagram, README UX for self-serve artifact
Eng (Runtime): build minimal proxy image and preflight script; expose telemetry hooks
Eng (Infra): publish artifact to internal downloads and get signed checksum
Security: run review on artifact, KMS guidance, and audit logging expectations
Support/SE: author runbook and define SLA per lane
Pilot: run two customer pilots, collect telemetry and feedback
Metrics: instrument intake spreadsheet to capture reason codes + time-to-provision
risks_and_tradeoffs: Providing a self-serve template reduces gate friction but increases support requests for edge cases — mitigated by clear disclaimers and an FAQ
A minimal proxy image risks missing enterprise hardening; require Security signoff and optional hardened variant
Automating lane assignment may misclassify nuanced requests — keep manual override path for SEs and legal
Telemetry footprint must be extremely small in air-gapped scenarios; design for push/pull variants and explicit opt-in
